subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime `sessions.patch` fail closed on legacy ownerless rows, even though upgrades may leave previously created plugin sessions unattributed?
rationale: No code path can safely infer which plugin owns an existing ownerless row; allowing adoption preserves compatibility by weakening the ownership boundary, while rejection may interrupt existing plugin workflows until an operator handles the row.

options.title: Fail closed on ownerless rows
options.body: Reject plugin-runtime patches when ownership is absent and document that an operator or non-plugin client must manage or recreate the legacy session.

options.title: Preserve ownerless compatibility
options.body: Continue allowing plugin-runtime patches to ownerless rows, accepting that any in-process plugin could claim or mutate unattributed legacy sessions.

options.title: Pause pending migration design
options.body: Do not land the restriction until maintainers define a trustworthy attribution or operator-assisted migration for legacy rows.

recommendation.title: Fail closed on ownerless rows
recommendation.body: Reject plugin-runtime patches when ownership is absent and document that an operator or non-plugin client must manage or recreate the legacy session.

likelyOwner.reason: The current ownership fence and session projection behavior trace to this contributor's recent merged work.
